title: Session ID can escape evidence storage directory
evidence: bundle_dir joins base_dir with caller-supplied session_id; audit() does not validate it. _write_bundle_manifest opens manifest.json and events.json with mode w.
trigger: Call audit(session_id="/an/existing/writable/directory") or use ../ components, then close().
impact: Evidence files are written outside storage_dir and existing files with those names are overwritten. Scope is caller-controlled IDs; no remote caller established.

title: Closed audit sessions still accept unsealed events
evidence: log_step acquires the lock but never checks is_closed. close() returns the old summary immediately on subsequent calls.
trigger: Call close(), then log_step(), or race a waiting logger with close().
impact: In-memory total_events changes after root/signature and disk events were sealed; later close/export cannot persist or reseal the added events.

title: Failed evidence persistence permanently marks session closed
evidence: close() sets is_closed=True before signing, hardware quote, and _write_bundle_manifest; a subsequent close() immediately returns get_summary().
trigger: Filesystem write fails during close(), then caller restores storage and retries close().
impact: Retry reports a closed session without retrying missing/partial evidence writes or registering completion.

title: AL0 and AL1 roots do not commit to their events
evidence: Only AL2/AL3 branches call accumulator.add_leaf. close() uses accumulator.finalize for any nonempty events; finalize returns the empty hash when no leaves exist.
trigger: Close two AL0 or AL1 sessions with different nonempty events.
impact: global_merkle_root/global_hash is the same empty-tree digest and does not bind event contents; AL1 prev_hash is not included in manifest or summary.

title: Claim pending messages atomically before delivering them
evidence: pull_messages SELECTs pending rows at 160-170 and later UPDATEs selected IDs at 198-205, without BEGIN IMMEDIATE or a conditional pending claim. mcp_server.py:290 exposes this as receive_messages.
trigger: Two consumers pull the same destination concurrently, before either UPDATE commits.
impact: Both can return the same pending messages, causing duplicate handling. This is a static interleaving finding; concurrent execution was not performed.

title: Persistent tunnel connections lower required durability to NORMAL
evidence: Every _get_connection executes PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; .babylon60rules requires transactional persistence with synchronous=FULL.
trigger: The broker acknowledges a committed message before a system power failure.
impact: Acknowledged WAL commits lack the required FULL synchronization guarantee. The audit did not simulate power loss.

title: Attestation lock acquisition is not atomic
evidence: _acquire_lock checks exists then opens with w; _release_lock removes the shared path.
trigger: Two attestor processes both pass exists before either creates the file.
impact: Both enter the supposedly exclusive section, and either can delete the lock while the other is still running.

title: Cached attestation tree hash survives HEAD changes
evidence: lru_cache key contains only path; git ls-tree HEAD is evaluated only on cache miss. generate_attestation_payload calls it with the same target_dir at line 50.
trigger: A long-lived Python process generates a payload, changes Git HEAD, then generates another for the same path.
impact: The new timestamp is paired with the previous tree digest, misidentifying the version being attested.

title: Array display truncation corrupts the GGUF parse cursor
evidence: The ARRAY branch consumes count.min(10) values then returns that cursor, without skipping remaining elements.
trigger: Load a valid GGUF metadata array containing more than ten elements, such as tokenizer vocabulary.
impact: The next metadata key or tensor descriptor is read from inside the array; ordinary models fail to load or receive incorrect descriptors.

title: Truncated GGUF metadata panics instead of returning an error
evidence: parse_metadata_value directly indexes mmap[cursor] and slices cursor..cursor+N; caller checks the type tag but not its payload.
trigger: A file ends immediately after a UINT8 metadata type tag, or contains a truncated string/scalar payload.
impact: Untrusted model input can panic the inference process rather than produce load_mmap Err.

title: Path import inserted before __future__ imports makes rewritten modules invalid
evidence: ensure_pathlib_import inserts at index 0 or 1 (docstring only), without skipping future imports; heal_file writes ast.unparse output without compilation.
trigger: A module containing from __future__ import annotations and a matching home-path literal, without an existing Path import.
impact: The remediation writes an import ahead of __future__, causing SyntaxError when the rewritten module is imported.

title: Existing pathlib import incorrectly treated as a bound Path name
evidence: import pathlib and from pathlib import Path as P both set has_pathlib=True, while visit_Constant generates unqualified Path.home().
trigger: A rewritten module uses import pathlib (or aliases Path) without independently binding Path.
impact: Generated path expressions raise NameError, breaking code the remediation claims to repair.

title: Dry-run still overwrites the session log
evidence: --dry-run promises no writing (line 253); main unconditionally calls _generate_anagnorisis_log, whose lines 197-199 write ANAGNORISIS_LOG.md without a dry_run argument.
trigger: Run --dry-run --term with --artifact-dir pointing at an existing directory.
impact: Preview mode creates or overwrites a persistent session artifact.

title: Replacing phase 2f deletes all subsequent skill sections
evidence: The replacement pattern \n\n### Fase 2f:.* uses re.DOTALL and is not bounded by the next heading before write_text at line 172.
trigger: Update a skill containing an existing phase 2f followed by another section.
impact: All content following phase 2f is discarded, including unrelated instructions.

title: Escape user-controlled values before producing YAML
evidence: Topic and decision strings are interpolated directly into double-quoted YAML scalars (lines 41-44,50).
trigger: run_grill_you(topic=...) receives a topic containing a quote, backslash or newline.
impact: to_yaml() can return invalid YAML or injected YAML fields rather than faithfully serializing the supplied topic. No downstream privileged YAML consumer was established.

title: Drug-target affinity cancels the target vector
evidence: bind multiplies bipolar components (56-58); similarity dots them (60-63); affinity returns dot(drug*target,target)/DIMENSION (112-119). Since target_i squared is 1, result is sum(drug_i)/DIMENSION.
trigger: Compute affinity for the same drug against any two registered targets.
impact: All targets receive the same affinity, so this method cannot rank target-specific interactions; this is an algebraic software defect, not a clinical outcome claim.

title: Do not approve JavaScript solely from balanced delimiters
evidence: For JavaScript/TypeScript validate_syntax returns True after delimiter matching alone, e.g. const x = ; contains no unbalanced delimiter; zero_token_feedback_loop maps True to APPROVED. Targeted search found only tests consuming these APIs, no production executor.
trigger: Call syntax feedback on invalid JavaScript with balanced delimiters.
impact: The public validation API claims syntax approval for non-parsing source; no authorization bypass or actual execution is established.

title: WAL write failure is swallowed after state has changed
evidence: transition_to changes current_state at 115 before callback 118–119; _log_causal_event catches IOError and only logs at 207–208. spawn similarly returns after the callback.
trigger: Filesystem write/flush/fsync fails during a transition, including POISONED.
impact: Caller receives success but restart restores the older state, potentially losing a terminal poison state.

title: Formal model proofs are presented as absolute physical runtime guarantees
evidence: The Lean section states that model verification makes torn reads physically impossible and certifies the absolute mathematical validity of the code. Its cited sources define and prove properties of Lean traces (BabylonTrace.lean:156 and AX0.lean:144); the section provides no implementation refinement proof or platform memory-model assumptions.
trigger: Use the research document to assess the guarantee provided by compiling the cited Lean files.
impact: Readers are led to treat a model-level theorem as certification of the deployed implementation; scope must distinguish the modeled transition system from Rust/OS/hardware execution.

title: Generate calibration constants in the module actually compiled
evidence: __file__ lives in scripts/c5_calibrations; joining .. / src writes scripts/src/generated_aphairesis_constants.rs. src/lib.rs:71 instead loads repository src/generated_aphairesis_constants.rs.
trigger: Run the documented calibration generator.
impact: Compiled constants remain stale while the command reports successful generation.

title: Use a wider mask for the advertised eight-sample boundary
evidence: The API advertises n<=8 at 41 and debug_asserts n<=8 at 45, but builds the mask with (1u8 << n)-1 at 63.
trigger: cluster_and_compute_entropy is called with n=8, which its public contract admits.
impact: Shifting an eight-bit integer by eight overflows; checked builds panic and unchecked execution cannot form the required 0xff domain mask, invalidating the advertised boundary.

title: Extractor promotes a satisfiable assumption set without checking the trace cluster
evidence: Only traces[0] supplies files_count (lines 65–66); solver constraints assert that value and EXIT_CODE=0 and check satisfiability. No other trace is checked against that count. The result is persisted as EXTRACTED at lines 99–106. proof_emitter_lean4.py:166–196 consumes EXTRACTED and independently selects LIMIT 1; codegen_rust_b60.py:39–64 subsequently uses first-trace cardinality for dispatch.
trigger: Successful traces in the same AST cluster touch different numbers of files.
impact: A first-sample property is recorded as a cluster invariant and propagated into generated proof/dispatch artifacts; this is not evidence of an authorization bypass.

title: Staged canary deletion is accepted when the file remains locally
evidence: Failure requires path absent from git ls-files AND Path(path).exists()==False; pre-commit-config.yaml:42-46 installs this as a commit guard.
trigger: Remove a declared planted canary from the Git index while retaining its working-tree file.
impact: The commit guard passes although the committed tree no longer contains the declared canary, contradicting its index-integrity purpose.

title: Full-spectrum auditor emits PASS and certified measurements without performing checks
evidence: audit_cohort_ring0 sets PASS and assigns atomic/concurrency/biometric claims as strings (lines 80 onward). Formal cohort likewise assigns certification strings; linguistic entropy is a constant (ent=4.967), not calc_shannon_entropy. run_100_agents_audit aggregates these verdicts and persists them as a SITREP.
trigger: Run the advertised audit against a broken or unverified implementation.
impact: Audit artifact claims successful security/formal/physical verification even though the relevant implementation and measurements were never inspected.

title: Branch protection enforcement suppresses API failures
evidence: gh api PUT failure is handled by || echo; execution then reaches the success-style dispatched message and exits successfully. Missing gh also exits 0 at line 14.
trigger: GitHub rejects the branch protection request or gh is unavailable.
impact: Automation can treat enforcement as successful while required branch protections were never applied.

title: Differential comparison reads both artifacts after the Rust run
evidence: Rust .output() completes at lines 31-33 before py_ir is read at line 47; rs_ir is then read from the same artifact_bundle_v3/proof.ir at line 51. src/babylon60.rs:594 writes that path. Cargo.toml:76-77 registers this test.
trigger: Reference interpreter exists and both commands complete successfully.
impact: The comparison can hash the Rust-produced artifact twice and pass despite a different Python trace. Currently the missing reference/interpreter.py also causes an early successful return at lines 15-18.

title: Retain failed batch items instead of removing the entire batch
evidence: Promise.allSettled records rejected fetches at line 72, then line 74 always stores queueData.slice(100); fulfilled HTTP error responses are also counted as processed.
trigger: Any of the first 100 requests rejects or returns an unsuccessful HTTP status.
impact: Copying this documented batch processing pattern permanently discards failed work with no retry.

title: Extension scan misses wildcard content-script injections
evidence: hit_matches uses domain in m and reports no extension intercepts domain when no literal substring matches (143,152-153).
trigger: Scan example.com while an extension declares <all_urls> or *://*/*.
impact: Tool reports no intercepting extension although a broad match pattern includes the requested domain, undermining forensic triage.

title: Comment fallback directs audit output without acquiring comments
evidence: On extraction failure, Phase 3b directs generation of SOCINT audit by projecting five vectors from predictable audience sociology (201–203).
trigger: A comments audit cannot retrieve comments within 10 seconds or encounters anti-bot/error responses.
impact: The prescribed fallback substitutes imagined audience reactions for unavailable observations; no explicit labeling requirement separates projections from an actual comments audit.
